> **Pipeline step 04 — collinearity screen.**
>
> **Purpose.** Pearson correlation matrices (scatter + lowess below the diagonal, r with
> significance stars above, histograms on the diagonal) for every z-scored covariate, one figure
> per survey x water year, at 174 mm with an 8 pt floor on every label.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv`, `data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv`.
> **Outputs.** `output_figs/corr_tps_WY<year>.{pdf,tiff,png}`, `output_figs/corr_edsm_WY<year>.{pdf,tiff,png}`.
>
> (Moved verbatim from section 7 of `03_tps_forklength_models/gear_check_mamou_vs_otter.Rmd`.)

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```

```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
dir.create("output_figs", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Covariate correlation matrices (TPS and EDSM, by water year)

Diagnostic for the main modelling frames: one pairs-plot correlation matrix per survey and
water year, over every z-scored covariate in the model dataset plus day of water year. Used to
screen collinearity before building the model sets (e.g. temperature tracks `water_year_day`
at r = 0.75-0.95 in every year, so it was left out of the main sets).

`chart.Correlation()` is base graphics built on `pairs()`, so it cannot be
faceted the way a ggplot can. The equivalent is one matrix per water year, drawn
in a loop.

**On the 8 pt minimum.** `PerformanceAnalytics::chart.Correlation()` cannot be
made to respect a floor through its arguments: it sizes each correlation number
as `cex * (abs(r) + 0.3) / 1.3`, so a near-zero r renders at ~23% of the base
size no matter what `cex.cor` is passed. `chart_corr8()` below is a drop-in
replacement using the same `pairs()` layout and the same panels, with every
`cex` floored at `MIN_CEX`. Devices are opened with `pointsize = 8`, so
`cex = 1` is exactly 8 pt and nothing can render smaller; the emphasis-by-|r|
effect is kept, it just scales upward from 8 pt instead of downward.

```{r corr-setup, message=FALSE}
tps_wq  <- read.csv("data/tow_12_6_tps_wq_nona.csv")
edsm_wq <- read.csv("data/tow_12_6_edsm_wq_nona.csv")

# every z-scored covariate present, plus day of water year
covar_cols <- function(df) {
  cols <- grep("_z$|^water_year_day$", names(df), value = TRUE)
  # Older copies of the model CSVs carry an annual (one value per water year) index that is
  # not a covariate in any reported model; keep it out of the matrices if present.
  cols[!grepl("spawner", cols)]
}

MIN_CEX  <- 1   # x device pointsize; devices below are opened at pointsize = 8
PT       <- 8

covar_cols(tps_wq)
covar_cols(edsm_wq)
```

```{r corr-fun}
chart_corr8 <- function(d, main = "", method = "pearson") {

  panel_cor <- function(x, y, digits = 2, ...) {
    usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr = usr)); par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
    r    <- cor(x, y, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = method)
    txt  <- format(c(r, 0.123456789), digits = digits)[1]
    base <- 0.8 / strwidth(txt)               # size that fills ~80% of the panel
    # keep chart.Correlation's emphasis-by-|r|, but never shrink below MIN_CEX
    text(0.5, 0.5, txt, cex = max(MIN_CEX, base * (abs(r) + 0.3) / 1.3))
    p   <- suppressWarnings(
             cor.test(as.numeric(x), as.numeric(y), method = method)$p.value)
    sig <- symnum(p, corr = FALSE, na = FALSE,
                  cutpoints = c(0, .001, .01, .05, .1, 1),
                  symbols   = c("***", "**", "*", ".", " "))
    text(0.82, 0.82, sig, cex = max(MIN_CEX, base * 0.7), col = 2)
  }

  panel_smooth <- function(x, y, col = "black", bg = NA, pch = 19, cex = 0.35,
                           col.smooth = "red", span = 2/3, iter = 3, ...) {
    points(x, y, pch = pch, col = col, bg = bg, cex = cex)
    ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
    if (any(ok))
      lines(stats::lowess(x[ok], y[ok], f = span, iter = iter), col = col.smooth)
  }

  panel_hist <- function(x, ...) {
    usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr = usr)); par(usr = c(usr[1:2], 0, 1.5))
    h  <- hist(x, plot = FALSE); br <- h$breaks; nB <- length(br)
    rect(br[-nB], 0, br[-1], h$counts / max(h$counts),
         col = "grey85", border = "grey40")
    tryCatch({
      dn <- density(x, na.rm = TRUE, adjust = 1.2)
      lines(dn$x, dn$y / max(dn$y), col = "red", lwd = 1)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    rug(x)
  }

  pairs(d, gap = 0, main = main,
        oma = c(4, 4, 8, 4),           # top margin widened for the 2-line title
        cex.axis   = MIN_CEX,          # tick labels
        cex.labels = MIN_CEX,          # variable names on the diagonal
        cex.main   = MIN_CEX * 1.25,
        lower.panel = panel_smooth,
        upper.panel = panel_cor,
        diag.panel  = panel_hist)
}

# Display-only labels: the two distance names are too long to fit a diagonal
# panel at 174 mm / 8 pt. Applied at plot time; the data columns are untouched.
display_names <- function(nms) {
  nms <- sub("^distance_along_channel_z$", "dist_along_chan_z", nms)
  nms <- sub("^distance_m_z$",             "dist_off_chan_z",   nms)
  # dist_along_chan_z fills 94% of a diagonal panel and its trailing "_z" still
  # got clipped once the histogram is drawn, so the suffix comes off everything.
  # Every covariate here is z-scored anyway -- noted in the figure title instead.
  sub("_z$", "", nms)
}

chart_year <- function(df, yr, label) {
  d <- df[df$water_year == yr, covar_cols(df), drop = FALSE]
  # drop any column that is constant within this water year: a zero-variance column
  # makes the correlation undefined
  d <- d[, vapply(d, function(v) length(unique(v[!is.na(v)])) > 1, logical(1)),
         drop = FALSE]
  # display-only rename: the full name overflows its diagonal panel at 174 mm / 8 pt
  DISPLAY_NAMES <- c(distance_along_channel_z = "dist_along_chan")
  hit <- names(d) %in% names(DISPLAY_NAMES)
  names(d)[hit] <- DISPLAY_NAMES[names(d)[hit]]
  names(d) <- display_names(names(d))
  suppressWarnings(chart_corr8(
    d, main = sprintf("%s  -  water year %s  (n = %d tows)\nall covariates z-scored",
                      label, yr, nrow(d))))
  invisible(names(d))
}

# Draw to output_figs and inline; panel size scales with the number of covariates.
# 174 mm square: a correlation matrix is n x n panels, so the figure is square by
# construction and the double-column width sets both dimensions.
WIDTH_MM <- 174
DPI_TIFF <- 600

chart_year_saved <- function(df, yr, label, slug) {
  file <- sprintf("output_figs/corr_%s_WY%s", slug, yr)
  inch <- WIDTH_MM / 25.4

  pdf(paste0(file, ".pdf"), width = inch, height = inch, pointsize = PT)
  chart_year(df, yr, label); dev.off()

  # ragg, not grDevices::tiff(): on macOS the latter defaults to type = "quartz",
  # which warns "compression is not supported" and writes ~64 MB of uncompressed
  # RGBA per figure at 600 dpi. The cairo type would compress but needs XQuartz.
  # (ggsave() already routes TIFF through ragg, which is why the ggplot figures
  # in section 6 came out compressed.)
  if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) {
    ragg::agg_tiff(paste0(file, ".tiff"), width = WIDTH_MM, height = WIDTH_MM,
                   units = "mm", res = DPI_TIFF, compression = "lzw",
                   pointsize = PT)
  } else {
    tiff(paste0(file, ".tiff"), width = WIDTH_MM, height = WIDTH_MM,
         units = "mm", res = DPI_TIFF, compression = "lzw", pointsize = PT)
  }
  chart_year(df, yr, label); dev.off()

  png(paste0(file, ".png"), width = WIDTH_MM, height = WIDTH_MM, units = "mm",
      res = 150, pointsize = PT)
  chart_year(df, yr, label); dev.off()

  chart_year(df, yr, label)
}
```

## TPS

```{r corr-tps, fig.width=11, fig.height=11, results="hide", dev.args=list(pointsize=8)}
for (yr in sort(unique(tps_wq$water_year))) chart_year_saved(tps_wq, yr, "TPS", "tps")
```

## EDSM

```{r corr-edsm, fig.width=9, fig.height=9, results="hide", dev.args=list(pointsize=8)}
for (yr in sort(unique(edsm_wq$water_year))) chart_year_saved(edsm_wq, yr, "EDSM", "edsm")
```

```{r corr-files}
list.files("output_figs", pattern = "^corr_(tps|edsm)_WY", full.names = TRUE)
```
